brief:
Translate the given UI strings from English into id for a software product.
These are short UI microcopy strings - button labels, headings, aria-labels, and one-line descriptions - in a design-tool web app called Lolly. Keep them as short as the source; this is UI chrome, not prose.
Register: Standard Bahasa Indonesia (Anda), contemporary app register - distinctly Indonesian, NOT Malaysian Malay; established Indonesian tech vocabulary (unduh/unggah where natural, common English loanwords where real Indonesian UIs use them); Latin script; Western digits.
Never translate these terms - copy them verbatim wherever they appear: "Lolly", "SUSE", "Geeko", "Content Credentials", "C2PA", "Pose Geeko", "Neurospicy".
Preserve every {placeholder} token exactly (same braces, same name, same count) - these are runtime interpolations, not prose.
Preserve any inline HTML exactly: the same tags, the same count, every attribute (href, target, rel) byte-for-byte, and every HTML entity (&, <). Translate only the human text around and between the tags - never a tag name, an attribute value, or the contents of a <code> element.
Preserve punctuation choices like → and & as-is where they read naturally in the target language; do not add explanatory text.
Match the source length and register. Do not pad or embellish.
Term-sense guidance - translate each of these by its stated sense, NEVER literally: "house style" = the organisation's OWN editorial/design standard, as in a publishing or fashion house - never a residence or home decor. Use the target language's established term for an organisation's style standard (German 'Hausstil', Turkish 'kurumsal stil'), or keep the English where local professionals do. | "house rules" = an organisation's standing working conventions - never the rules of a household. | "in-house" = done inside the organisation itself - never inside a building or dwelling. | "design house / fashion house / publishing house" = a company or atelier - never a physical building. | "powerhouse" = an idiom for something exceptionally capable - never a power station or building. | "house reader rule" = this codebase's own parser convention (never throws, null on bad input) - 'house' means the project, not a home.
Use a plain hyphen "-" for parenthetical dashes. Never use an em-dash or a spaced en-dash: they read as machine-written in this language. An UNSPACED en-dash inside a numeric or alphabetic range (0-1, A-Z) is correct and must be preserved as-is.
No Oxford comma before the final conjunction in a list. A comma before a conjunction that joins two main clauses is still correct - only the list-final one is wrong.
Return ONLY the JSON matching the given schema - one translation per input id, in the same order.

What each mark does, with an example
Which colour plays each part in every tool and export. Until a colour of the design system's own takes a role, the starter's stands in. Contrast is measured against the surface, APCA first.
[pause] puts silence before the next sentence. Add a number for the seconds, and a small one runs two sentences together.
[slow] and [fast] change the pace of the sentence they sit in. These are the biggest levers you have.
